gates.claim: sum_j arg(1 - x y_j) = phi EXACTLY along the whole arc, endpoint included. Since the sum is congruent to phi mod 2 pi automatically (from the proved Vieta product), this says the branch integer k is 0 -- which is what hcont is used to establish
OBLIGATION 1 (replaces part of hcont): every arg(1 - x y_j) > -pi/2 on the open arc. Measured minimum -1.4077 against -pi/2 = -1.5708 -- a 10% margin, which is not generous

OBLIGATION 2: AT MOST ONE arg exceeds pi/2. Measured max count 1, and the second-largest arg peaks at 1.3099 against pi/2 = 1.5708 -- a 17% margin. This is what gives the upper bound sum < pi + pi/2 + pi/2 = 2 pi
OBLIGATION 3: at most TWO args are negative, i.e. at least one is >= 0. With G2 this gives the lower bound sum > 2*(-pi/2) + 0 = -pi

a structural simplification: on the OPEN arc the two log-sums are complex CONJUGATES, because the roots are closed under conjugation (real cubic on |x| = 1) and 1/x = conj x. Hence k_2 = -k_1 -- there is only ONE branch integer, not two. It holds to 1e-40 on [0,pi) and also at the endpoint here, though the argument for it breaks there since 1 - x y_1 sits on the cut

RULED OUT, recorded so it is not retried: the tempting route 'Re(1 - x y_j) > 0 on the arc, hence every |arg| < pi/2' is FALSE. max Re(x y_j) reaches 2.2468 already at phi/pi = 0.9975, so Re(1 - x y_j) goes negative near the endpoint. That is why G3 has to say 'at most one exceeds pi/2' rather than 'none does'

verdict.the_trade: hcont (continuity of the branch difference along the arc) is replaced by three real-algebraic inequalities on |x| = 1 -- G2, G3, G4 -- of the same shape as xy_neg, which this branch already proves by resultant elimination. The arithmetic that turns those bounds into k = 0 is Lean-proved (branchInt_eq_zero_of_arg_structure).
verdict.what_it_costs: the margins are not generous: -1.4077 vs -pi/2 is 10%, 1.3099 vs pi/2 is 17%. The eliminations will be tighter than xy_neg's. Whether the trade is worth making is a judgement, not a theorem.
verdict.bonus: G5: on the open arc the two log-sums are complex conjugates, so k_2 = -k_1 and there is only ONE branch integer to pin, not two.
verdict.ruled_out: G6: Re(1 - x y_j) > 0 does NOT hold on the arc -- it fails near the endpoint. Recorded so the route is not retried.
verdict.still_open: the three inequalities themselves. This probe does not prove them; it measures them and prices the trade.
